response.initial_request: The radiators have stopped heating intermittently. Hot water is still available. Please arrange an inspection.

other_sections.Attachments:
- [Copper Finch Mechanical — Invoice NBL-CFM-250210-A](attachments/invoice-NBL-CFM-250210-A.pdf)
- [Copper Finch Mechanical — Invoice NBL-CFM-250210-B](attachments/invoice-NBL-CFM-250210-B.pdf)

events.body: Reported that radiator heating had cut out twice since the previous evening while hot water remained available. A child lives at the property. Asked for an inspection.
Acknowledged the report and asked about leaks, unusual smells, boiler warnings and access times. No entry arrangement was yet confirmed.
Confirmed no visible leak, unusual smell or current warning light. The boiler had shown a brief symbol the previous night, but she did not identify it. She can provide access after 14:00 on weekdays.
Requested approval for a diagnostic visit. Noted that the agency's routine repair limit is £180 including VAT and that work above that limit needs landlord approval.
Authorized diagnosis up to £180 including VAT only. Asked to be consulted before any remedial work or additional expenditure is authorized.

Requested diagnosis of intermittent radiator heating, a written report and an itemized estimate before work beyond diagnosis. Confirmed access after 14:00 and the diagnostic-only authorization ceiling of £180 including VAT.
Confirmed attendance for 5 February after 14:00. Quoted £138 including VAT for attendance, diagnosis and testing; parts and remedial work were excluded.

Reported attending and finding an intermittent fault at the heating valve actuator. Said the heating operated during the visit and that no leak or immediate gas-safety concern was observed. No remedial work was reported in this update.

Sent an estimate for £372 including VAT for actuator supply and replacement, attendance and heating-system testing. Requested written authorization before proceeding. The estimate did not say whether the £138 diagnostic charge would be credited.

Forwarded the estimate and asked whether the proposed work was authorized. Noted that it exceeded the routine limit and that the contractor had been told to obtain written authorization before remedial work.
Reported that the radiators were cold again. She was using one portable heater in the sitting room and said it was plugged directly into a wall socket. No new smell, leak or warning was reported.
Had not decided on the estimate. Asked whether the actuator could be repaired and whether the price included all parts, labour and testing. Did not authorize remedial work or further expenditure.
Asked whether heating or safety symptoms had changed, whether the equipment-label details were available, and whether the contractor could be given access if a return visit were arranged.
Said the radiators were still inconsistent and repeated that hot water was available. Supplied the boiler-label details in the message. She had not agreed a return appointment.
Asked for a repair alternative, confirmation of parts availability, a breakdown of the estimate and clarification of whether diagnosis would be credited. Repeated that no further work was authorized.
Replied that parts availability and estimate details still needed checking. Did not confirm a repair option, a credit, a return visit or completion of actuator work.

Sent two invoice records dated 10 February and said they had been prepared from the job paperwork. The message did not say whether one replaced the other, whether both amounts were payable, or whether either had been paid. Invoice B describes actuator work as completed and gives a service date of 5 February, but Petra did not attach a signed completion record or explain how that claim relates to the estimate sent later on 5 February and the 7 February parts check.

The received invoice records list £138 for attendance, diagnosis, actuator inspection and an operational test, and £372 for actuator supply/replacement, attendance, diagnosis and heating-system testing. Both records identify 5 February as the service date. The second record's wider description includes activities also listed on the first; neither record states whether the other is credited, cancelled or superseded.

Compared the received records with the file: the landlord's written authority covers diagnosis only; the £372 estimate requesting authorization was sent after the stated service date; and the 7 February exchange still had parts and estimate details outstanding. The file contains no written authorization for actuator replacement and no return-visit or completion entry.

Said she recalled the 5 February visit but did not know whether the actuator had been replaced. She had not seen a contractor at the property since that visit. Heating was currently working intermittently, with one radiator cooler than the others.

Asked what work was actually completed and on what date, whether both invoice records remained current, whether either superseded the other, and how the overlapping charges were treated. Requested the job notes, any parts record and any authorization or attendance evidence for actuator work.

Replied that she was checking the records and could not yet confirm whether the invoice entries represented separate chargeable work or whether one record replaced the other. She supplied no further completion evidence, revised invoice or parts confirmation.

The two invoice records remain on file; there is no recorded payment, confirmed supersession or authorization for actuator work. The tenant reports intermittent heating and has not confirmed replacement. Please advise how you wish to proceed on the unresolved records and whether any further work or expenditure is authorized.

args.reason: Contractor invoices contradict the file on whether actuator work was done, and £372 was never authorised. This is a money and record conflict that the agency should not decide alone.

handover_note.known: Property: 7 Larkspur Fold, Orvane Heath, ZZ1 1ZZ. The tenant reported intermittent radiator heating on 3 Feb, with hot water still working and a child in the home (events 1, 3). The landlord authorised diagnosis only, up to £180 including VAT, and asked to be consulted before any remedial work (event 5). Copper Finch Mechanical quoted £138 including VAT for diagnosis (event 7). It attended on 5 Feb and found an intermittent heating valve actuator fault, with no leak or gas-safety concern. It reported no remedial work (event 8). At 14:54 on 5 Feb it sent a £372 estimate for actuator replacement and asked for written authorisation (event 9). The landlord had not decided on it, asked whether the actuator could be repaired and whether the price was all-inclusive, and authorised nothing (event 12). On 7 Feb the contractor said parts and estimate details still needed checking (event 16). On 10 Feb it sent invoice A for £138 (diagnosis and test) and invoice B for £372 (actuator supply and replacement, attendance, diagnosis, testing). Both give a service date of 5 Feb (events 17-18; invoice-NBL-CFM-250210-A.pdf and invoice-NBL-CFM-250210-B.pdf). The file has no payment, no signed completion record, no return visit and no written authorisation for actuator work (event 19). The tenant does not know whether the actuator was replaced and has seen no contractor since 5 Feb. Heating is still intermittent, with one radiator cooler than the others (event 20).
handover_note.conflicts: Invoice B claims the actuator was replaced on 5 Feb. The £372 estimate was only sent after the visit on 5 Feb. On 7 Feb the contractor was still checking parts availability. The tenant has no knowledge of a replacement and the heating is still faulty. Invoice B repeats the attendance and diagnosis already in invoice A, so the two overlap. Neither invoice says whether the other is credited, cancelled or superseded. The contractor was asked twice (events 15, 21) and could not clarify or give evidence (events 16, 22). Invoice B at £372 is above the £180 limit and has no landlord approval. Sending both would total £510.
handover_note.done: I read all 23 events and both invoices. I approved no invoice, instructed no contractor and sent no payment forward. Event 23 (12 Feb) already asked the landlord how to proceed. No reply is on file.
handover_note.needed: 1) Decide how to treat the invoices. Invoice A for £138 sits within the £180 diagnosis authority, and invoice B for £372 is unauthorised and unevidenced. Neither should be paid, forwarded or deducted from rent until this is settled. 2) Press Copper Finch Mechanical for job notes, parts records and a written statement of what was done on 5 Feb, and for a corrected or withdrawn invoice. 3) Get the landlord's decision on the repair, including the repair alternative and an all-inclusive price. 4) Because a child lives there and the tenant is using a portable heater plugged directly into a wall socket (event 11), consider whether the heating fault needs more urgent action and whether to give the tenant safety advice.

args.summary: Escalated to the property manager. Invoice B (£372) claims actuator replacement on 5 Feb, but the file has no authorisation, no completion evidence and no return visit. Invoice A (£138) is within the diagnosis authority, but the two invoices overlap. The tenant says the heating is still faulty.
facts: Landlord authorised diagnosis only, up to £180 including VAT (event 5).
The £372 estimate was sent after the 5 Feb visit and asked for written authorisation (event 9).
Landlord had not decided on the estimate and authorised no further spend (event 12).
The contractor was still checking parts and estimate details on 7 Feb (event 16).
Invoices A (£138) and B (£372) are both dated 10 Feb with a service date of 5 Feb (events 17-18; invoice PDFs).
No signed completion record, no payment and no written authorisation for actuator work is on file (event 19).
The tenant does not know whether the actuator was replaced, and heating is still intermittent (event 20).
The contractor could not clarify or give evidence when asked on 11 Feb (events 21-22).
The landlord was asked how to proceed on 12 Feb and has not replied (event 23).
conflicts: Invoice B says actuator replacement was completed on 5 Feb, but the estimate was sent later that day, parts were unconfirmed on 7 Feb, and the tenant is unaware of any replacement.
Invoices A and B overlap on attendance and diagnosis, and neither says whether the other is credited or superseded.
Invoice B (£372) is above the £180 routine limit and has no landlord approval.
missing: Contractor job notes, parts record and signed completion evidence
Landlord's decision on the invoices and on any further work
Clarification of which invoice is current and whether the diagnosis charge is credited
options_rejected: Approve or forward invoice A or B: unauthorised, contradictory and overlapping.
Ask the contractor again: it has been asked twice and could not answer.
Wait on the landlord only: the money dispute and the safety angle need property manager judgement.
Instruct the actuator replacement: the landlord has not authorised it.
args.uncertainty: The landlord may reply to event 23 and settle the invoice question. It is unknown whether the actuator was replaced.
